units.spine: Market day packs the squares, and the stalls are there because the roads keep bringing the custom.
A garrison and a professional watch keep the order here, and both draw a wage from the town.
The quarrels people carry into the taverns here are seldom about money.
Warehouses here are kept in repair, and the people who own them take the town for a place that lasts.
Walls and gates here are kept sound, and nothing on them was built for show.
Armed men go up on the walls when they are wanted, and they have the look of having been up there before.
Children here are given the rules about the dark early, and the rules hold.
The watch answers what is reported to it, and what is never reported is never looked for.
Prices here hold steady, and no house in the trades is living on what it sold last.
The mages' guild does what is commonly wanted of it and is plain about what is beyond it.
Food is not something people here think about, and the city's grain stores are the reason.
The town sits on the way to somewhere else and makes a modest living out of the passing trade.
What the town cannot grow comes in by road, and the road is a condition of the town's living.
Rundgate is large enough that a man from one quarter is a stranger in the next.
The town's dealings with its neighbours are the ordinary ones, and nothing it carries now has bent them.
